title: 1965 AHSME Problem 33
statement: If the number \(15!,\) that is, \(15\cdot14\cdot13\cdots1,\) ends with \(k\) zeros when given to the base \(12\) and ends with \(h\) zeros when given to the base \(10,\) then \(k+h\) equals:

solutions.text:
The prime valuations are \[ \begin{gathered} v_2(15!)=11,\\ v_3(15!)=6,\\ v_5(15!)=3. \end{gathered} \] Hence \(k=\min(\lfloor\frac{11}{2}\rfloor,6)=5\) in base \(12,\) and \(h=\min(11,3)=3\) in base \(10.\) Thus \(k+h=8.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Count the powers of \(2,\) \(3,\) and \(5\) in \(15!\)
A base-\(12\) zero uses \(2^2\cdot3\), while a base-\(10\) zero uses \(2\cdot5\)
